gloss: to stop by, to drop in, to visit briefly

definitions.gloss: to stop by, to drop in
definitions.explanation: To visit a place briefly, usually on the way to somewhere else.
To move closer to someone or something, often with a sense of proximity or closeness.

examples.japanese: {帰|かえ}りにコンビニに{立|た}ち{寄|よ}った。
examples.english: I stopped by the convenience store on my way home.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くの{本屋|ほんや}に{立|た}ち{寄|よ}ってから{会社|かいしゃ}に{向|む}かった。
examples.english: I stopped by the bookstore near the station before heading to the office.

examples.japanese: {観光|かんこう}のついでに{有名|ゆうめい}な{神社|じんじゃ}に{立|た}ち{寄|よ}ったら、{思|おも}いがけず{美|うつく}しい{庭園|ていえん}を{見|み}ることができた。
examples.english: When I stopped by a famous shrine while sightseeing, I was able to see a beautiful garden unexpectedly.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}がそっと{立|た}ち{寄|よ}ってきた。
{知|し}らない{人|ひと}が{立|た}ち{寄|よ}ってきたので、{少|すこ}し{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: A stranger approached me, so I was a little surprised.

examples.japanese: {火|ひ}に{立|た}ち{寄|よ}ると{危|あぶ}ないから、{離|はな}れていなさい。
examples.english: It's dangerous to go near the fire, so stay away.

notes:
{立|た}ち{寄|よ}る is an intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}).

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
- {立|た}つ (to stand) + {寄|よ}る (to approach) → to stop and approach

SENSE 1 (to stop by):
ASPECT (ている): {立|た}ち{寄|よ}っている indicates being at a place one has stopped by.
COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～に{立|た}ち{寄|よ}る (stop by~)
- {帰|かえ}りに{立|た}ち{寄|よ}る (stop by on the way home)
- ついでに{立|た}ち{寄|よ}る (stop by while you're at it)
- お{立|た}ち{寄|よ}りください (please stop by - polite)

SENSE 2 (to approach, to draw near):
- ～に{立|た}ち{寄|よ}る (approach~, draw near to~)
- {立|た}ち{寄|よ}ってくる (come closer)

RELATED NOUN:
- {立|た}ち{寄|よ}り: a stop, stopover; {立|た}ち{寄|よ}り{先|さき} = place one stops by

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寄|よ}る: to stop by (simpler, more casual); also to approach
- {訪|たず}ねる: to visit (more formal, planned)

[Register: Neutral]
